never adverb

also never again, not ever

classical

Cic. Q. fr. 3.1.3: ego locum aestāte umbrōsiōrem vīdī numquam
Hor. S. 2.8.3–4: ut mihi numquam in vītā fuerit melius
Traupman 88

numquam

adverb

After “and”, Latin says nec umquam: mihi tē cārius nihil esse nec umquam fuisse (Cic. Fam. 14.3.5). Numquam nōn is “always” (see always).

Other words

  • numquam posthāc — never again

    also used · classical · Catull. 99.16 (Lewis & Short, s.v. posthāc)

    The Latin for “never again”.

Examples

  • ego locum aestāte umbrōsiōrem vīdī numquam

    I have never seen a shadier spot in summerCic. Q. fr. 3.1.3

  • cūrā ut valeās et ita tibi persuādeās, mihi tē cārius nihil esse nec umquam fuisse

    look after yourself, and be sure that nothing is or ever was dearer to me than youCic. Fam. 14.3.5

See also always, never mind, not yet, now.
